# Tools

What follows is the tool catalog: what the chat agent can call, where
each tool comes from, and how approval, read-only mode, and shell
disabling change the effective set.

Everything that runs is generic: the same function body is shared by
the TUI (the agent's own tool loop), the web UI (slash commands through
`POST /api/tool/execute`), and explicit agent runs.
Each tool returns a
human-readable string rather than a Python exception, so a failure
arrives in chat as an `error`-status message --- never as a traceback.

## 1. How the tool set is assembled

  | Layer                        | Source module                                           | When it attaches                                                                    | Filter switches                                                           |
  | ---------------------------- | -----------------------------------------------------   | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
  | Workspace file tools         | `berg_agents/agents/factory.py` (`create_tools`)        | Always in `WorkspaceToolset`                                                        | `read_only=True` hides mutating tools; `allow_shell=False` hides `bash`   |
  | Plan / implement delegates   | `berg_agents/agents/workspace_toolset.py`               | Non-read-only mode                                                                  | Uses `PlannerDeps` and `ImplementationDeps`                               |
  | Web helpers                  | `berg_agents/capabilities/web_backends.py`              | If `BERG_AGENT_WEB_SEARCH_BACKENDS` is configured to at least one working backend   | Backends without dependencies are skipped                                 |
  | Memory (notebook)            | `../berg_agents/capabilities/context_capabilities.py`   | When the `Memory` capability is available                                           | Degrades to SQLite if `FileStore` fails                                   |
  | Step persistence / recall    | Same as above                                           | When both `StepPersistence` and `ConversationSearch` load                           | Requires runs DB write access                                             |
  | MCP toolsets                 | `{config}/mcp.json` (configurable)                      | At startup, per server                                                              | Kill-switch (`enabled: false`), runtime enable/disable, sensitive gate    |
  | Skills                       | `BERG_AGENT_SKILLS`                                     | As deferred toolsets; body not attached to every call                               | Progressively loaded; tool metadata exposed as `berg-plugin-skill-*`      |
  | Plugin tools                 | Enabled plugins that register `ToolCapability`          | Each turn (live state)                                                              | "Plugin OFF" removes them next turn; `POST /api/plugins/{id}/disable`     |

On a given machine, confirm the exact tools by running
`/tools` in the chat UI or `GET /api/tools` in the web UI / curl.
The
`[Tools]` Slash command is always available.

## 2. Workspace tools

Defined in `berg_agents/agents/factory.py`; bound to the resolved
workspace (the configured web root is usually passed in
`BergAgentsApp.create()`).

Path normalization: arguments are workspace-relative; the `/workspace/`
prefix is accepted and normalized; `..`, `~`, or anything outside the root
is rejected.

  | Tool               | Risk class   | Signature                                                           | Notes                                                                                                        |
  | ------------------ | ------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
  | `list_files`       | low          | `list_files(file_path: str = ".") -> str`                           | Bounded recursive listing; skips `.git`, `node_modules`, `__pycache__`, `.venv`, `.next`, `dist`, `.turbo`   |
  | `read_file`        | low          | `read_file(file_path: str) -> str`                                  | `ValueError` path errors are reported as strings                                                             |
  | `search_code`      | low          | `search_code(pattern: str, directory: str = ".") -> str`            | Simple string substring match; 50 hit cap, 2000 scanned files, 1M file size limit                            |
  | `bash`             | high         | `bash(command: str, timeout: int = 30) -> str`                      | Runs with `stderr=STDOUT` inside the workspace root; requires approval                                       |
  | `edit_file`        | high         | `edit_file(file_path: str, content: str) -> str`                    | Whole-file overwrite (see *Harness note* below)                                                              |
  | `patch_file`       | high         | `patch_file(file_path: str, old_text: str, new_text: str) -> str`   | Single contiguous replacement; target occurrence count must be 1                                             |
  | `write_file`       | high         | `write_file(file_path: str, content: str) -> str`                   | Create/overwrite using atomic writes                                                                         |
  | `plan_task`        | low          | `plan_task(description: str) -> str`                                | Read-only, isolated planner agent (`PlannerDeps`); call this before any multi-step `implement_task`          |
  | `implement_task`   | high         | `implement_task(plan: str, task_type: str = "generic") -> str`      | Isolated implementation agent with workspace tools; needs explicit user approval before use                  |

Risk class maps directly to HITL policy: **low** runs without approval; **high** pauses for a HITL round-trip (TUI
prompt or web Approve/Reject/
Edit).
Restricting mutating tools is supported in two ways:

- Read-only mode (`read_only=True`) drops every mutating tool at
  registration, not only with prompting.
- `allow_shell=False` drops `bash`.
  Both are per-deployment flags.

### Path safety

All file tools resolve inside the workspace root (`..`, `~`, and absolute
paths outside the root are rejected).
Atomic writes and the normalization
helper live in `berg_agents/tools/_io.py`.

## 3. Web tools

Berg-agents ships two web tools for search and fetch, both built over a
registered backend list (`BERG_AGENT_WEB_SEARCH_BACKENDS`).
Defaults:
`["ollama", "duckduckgo", "direct"]`.

| Backend name | Keyword var | Search | Fetch | Behaviour |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ollama` | `OLLAMA_API_KEY` | ✓ | ✓ | Ollama search index + API fetch (returns prompt with attached content) |
| `duckduckgo` | none | ✓ | ✗ | No-key fallback for search only |
| `direct` | none | ✗ | ✓ | Universal HTTP fetch; user-agent identifies BergAgents as a browser |

Functions exposed to the agent:
- `web_search(query: str, max_results: int = 5)` --- clamped to 1--10;
silently skips broken backends and returns a "no results/set OLLAMA_API_KEY"
message if none succeed.
- `web_fetch(url: str)` --- fetches one page through the first backend that
supports fetch.

Unknown backend names warn and are skipped, not fatal.
See `CONFIGURATION`
for the backend list config.

## 4. Memory tools

Provided by pydantic AI harness `Memory` capability over `FileStore` or a
SQLite fallback when `FileStore` fails.
Notebook name: `MEMORY.md` in
`{config}/memory/`.
Per-project isolation is derived from owning the
config directory; no namespace is used.

  | Tool             | Shape                                                        | What it does                                                       |
  | ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------ |
  | `write_memory`   | `write_memory(content, file=MAIN_FILENAME, old_text=None)`   | Append by default; replace exact once via `old_text` (pass empty   |
`content` to delete a passage); file size enforced through
`max_memory_size` (~ truncation) \|
\| `read_memory` \| `read_memory(file: str)` \| Returns a bounded excerpt of a **topic file**; do NOT use for
`MEMORY.md` (already injected, lives outside the workspace) \|
\| `search_memory` \| `search_memory(query: str)` \| Bounded keyword search across memory files (snippet-shaped
response) \|
\| `delete_memory` \| `delete_memory(file: str)` \| Removes the entire memory file \|

Memory snapshot (the main notebook) is injected at *every* request inside
`<memory>...</memory>` + `<memory_instructions>`.
Its guidance explicitly
says the agent does not re-read `MEMORY.md`.
Token budget is governed by
`max_tokens`/`max_lines`.

See [Memory & Compaction](MEMORY.qmd).

## 5. Persistence and recall tools

Two capabilities together provide history recall:

- `StepPersistence` (`SqliteStepStore`, `{config}/runs.db`) snapshots
  every settled step.
- `ConversationSearch` (over the same store, scope `conversation`)
  gives a keyword-searchable prefix query over steps previously
  compacted away.

They share one store so a compacted turn stays recoverable.
Neither
capability adds a directly callable tool; they act through the system
prompt on every turn.

## 6. MCP toolsets

External MCP servers are declared in `{config}/mcp.json` (path
configurable via `BERG_AGENT_MCP_SERVERS`).
They add tools prefixed by
`{server_name}_` to avoid clashes.
Both transports are supported:

- `stdio` (command + args + env)
- `http` (url + headers)

Gating:
- *sensitive* servers (e.g. `github`, `memory`) pause for HITL
- *read-only* and `context7`/`docs`/`reference` run without interruption
- **Kill-switch**: `"enabled": false` in each entry.
(Config is the
startup default only --- runtime state is authoritative, UI toggles take
over per turn.)
- Co-existence with agents: the same server appears as
`berg-plugin-mcp-*` in `/api/plugins` so the 🧩 Plugins browser shows
its transport + approval flag.

## 7. Skills (deferred)

`BERG_AGENT_SKILLS` is a JSON array of paths pointing at `SKILL.md`
directories.
Each skill is wrapped as a plugin (`berg-plugin-skill-*`) and
exposed as a **deferred toolset** --- a guidance text telling the model how
to load the body, without attaching it to every turn.
This reduces token
pressure while still giving access to heavy specialized prompts.
They are
not re-initialized mid-run once started.
Input format accepts paths or `[path, label]` pairs (new library-skills
syntax).

## 8. Plugin tools

A plugin that registers `ToolCapability` entries has its tool (s) parsed
into the chat path every turn, tied to its enabled state.

Calling paths (two surfaces):

1. Through chat: normal model → tool calling.
2. Through UI (and `/api` clients):
   `POST /api/plugins/{plugin_id}/tools/{tool_name}`
   - valid plugin, must exist + be enabled
   - tool match = either advertised name or function `__name__` so
     non-model helpers (e.g. `list_todo_items`) stay callable
   - run with the project as cwd
   - non-string values JSON-encoded; strings returned directly
   - 404 for unknown plugin/tool in any state.

Full conformance example: shared-todo (` plugins/SHARED-TODO.qmd`).

## 9. Approval, safety & hardening

- **HITL interaction in Python**: approvals get a system message + a
  retry prompt; auto-rejected orphaned approvals produce a dismissible
  alert plus retriable reason in the UI.
- **Read-only deployments**: mutating tools vanish from the tool schema,
  which is stronger than "ask the model not to".
  Write-path tests,
  end-to-end, do the same.
- **Bash timeout** default 30s, bounded per invocation.
- **Workspace escape** denied by path wrapper.
- **MCP safety**: sensitive servers trigger a pause; confidential tokens
  only via `${env:VAR}` placeholders (never literal secrets).
- **Risk metadata** flows from each `ToolSpec`; surface surfaces them in
  the web UI tool list (risk class labels).

## 10. Tool execute API

`GET  /api/tools` --- tool names and risk classes.
`POST /api/tool/execute` --- execute one tool in-band; body
`{ "tool": "...", "args": { "file_path": "..." } }` (args may also be a
string treated as `file_path`).
Returns `ToolExecuteResponse`.
Used by
slash commands typed into the chat box (`/read_file foo` → tool call).

Tool outcomes feed learning stats (`GET /api/learning-stats`).
`run_task` is special-cased to launch a full harness task.

## 11. How to add a new tool

1. Implement the function in `berg_agents/agents/` (or plugin).
2. Wrap with `make_tool_spec(... name=..., risk_class=low|high ...)`.
3. Add it to `create_tools()` (and `plan_task`/`implement_task` are
   special-cased manual additions).
4. Use `ToolSpec` wrapper atomic operations (do not bypass).
5. Tests: unit + offline mocks; no live model; test both read-only +
   shell-disabled filter results when adding destructive tools.
6. docs (`TOOLS.qmd`) + configuration notes if it needs env keys.
